## PDF page 174

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=174)

```text
               ISOLATING 2 LIMPERS


Now you will look at spots with two limpers.

Each exercise contains information about the action and ranges for both
players. Start by filling out the %-form for the limping and continuance ranges
of both opponents.

Then answer the question below. You can calculate how often both players
will fold manually or use the “Multiple Folders” spreadsheet.

Like in previous chapters, these defense ranges are simplified to make your
life easier. I would consider it unlikely that the open-limper is apt to tighten
up their continuance range, even though they do not close the action, since
open-limping is not traditionally the mark of a solid player. However, the
second player may continue a little differently dependent upon the open-
limper’s action. These simplified range ideas are useful and get you “close
enough”, but are not 100% precise in practice.

When doing these exercises, consider what would be the weakest pocket
pair you would isolate both limpers with given the assigned ranges. Would
you isolate with every Ax hand, or just some of them? What about Broadway
hands?

GLGL.




                                   PA G E 1 74
```
